context:
Theme ID: THEME-001
Theme Name: Digital Customer Onboarding Modernization

Theme Summary:
The organization wants to modernize the retail customer onboarding journey for new deposit-account customers. The current process is fragmented across web forms, call-center follow-up, and manual back-office verification. Customers frequently abandon registration when identity verification fails or when they cannot tell what step remains. Operations teams also spend significant time manually reviewing standard applications that could be handled automatically.

Business Need:
The target experience should let an eligible customer begin and complete onboarding digitally without contacting support. Identity verification should be automated for standard-risk applicants, while exceptions should be routed for manual review. Customers should be able to save progress and resume later without losing previously entered information. The journey should clearly show current status, remaining steps, and whether additional information is required.

Operational Expectations:
Manual verification effort should be reduced by 40%. Average end-to-end onboarding time for standard applications should be reduced by 25%. The number of abandoned applications should be reduced by at least 20% relative to the current baseline. When an application requires manual review, the customer should receive a clear status rather than seeing a generic error.

Customer Communication:
Customers should receive confirmation when an application is submitted successfully. If additional documentation is required, they should be told what is missing and how to provide it. When onboarding completes, the customer should receive a completion notification. Status information should be available in near real time.

Constraints:
The existing enterprise identity provider must remain in place. Existing KYC/AML policy rules must continue to apply. No additional mandatory phone call should be introduced into the standard onboarding path. Sensitive identity data must not be exposed in user-visible status messages.

Measures of Success:
- Reduce standard onboarding time by 25%.
- Reduce manual verification effort by 40%.
- Reduce abandoned applications by at least 20%.
- Preserve the current identity provider and compliance policy controls.
- Improve transparency by showing meaningful onboarding status and next steps.
output:
Title: Modernize Digital Customer Onboarding

Description:
Create a unified digital onboarding journey that allows eligible customers to complete standard account onboarding without contacting support. The experience will automate identity verification for standard-risk applicants, retain the existing enterprise identity provider and KYC/AML controls, and route verification exceptions to manual review. Customers can save an incomplete application and resume later without re-entering completed information. The journey will provide meaningful near-real-time status, remaining steps, and clear requests for additional documentation without exposing sensitive identity information.

Success Criteria:
- Standard application onboarding time is reduced by 25%.
- Manual verification effort is reduced by 40%.
- Abandoned applications are reduced by at least 20%.
- Standard-risk identity verification is automated and exceptions are routed to manual review.
- Customers can save and resume onboarding without losing previously entered data.
- Customers can see meaningful status, remaining steps, and required actions.
- Customers receive confirmation after submission, notification when documentation is required, and notification when onboarding completes.
- The existing identity provider and current KYC/AML controls remain in use.
- No mandatory phone call is introduced into the standard onboarding path.
- Sensitive identity details are not exposed in customer-facing status messages.

context:
Theme ID: THEME-002
Theme Name: Insurance Claims Triage and Review Acceleration

Theme Summary:
Claims operations teams are struggling with long review cycles, inconsistent triage, and excessive manual work for low-risk claims. The objective is to improve the speed of claim handling without weakening fraud controls or reducing the quality of review.

Business Need:
Incoming claims should be categorized by risk and complexity using available claim attributes. Low-risk claims should be routed into a fast-track process, while high-risk or suspicious claims should be escalated for senior review. Reviewers need clear visibility into why a claim was escalated, what information is missing, and what action is required next.

Operational Expectations:
Average claims review time should be reduced by 30%. At least 90% of eligible low-risk claims should receive a decision within 2 business days. Manual rework caused by incomplete or misrouted claims should remain below 5%. High-risk claims should not be automatically approved.

Customer Experience:
Customers should be informed when a claim is received, when more information is required, and when a decision is made. Notifications must use plain language and must not expose internal fraud-scoring logic.

Reviewer Experience:
Reviewers should see a prioritized work queue with the claim risk category, aging information, missing documents, and escalation reason. They should be able to add notes and reassign a claim when necessary.

Constraints:
Existing policy administration and fraud systems remain systems of record. The new workflow may orchestrate work but must not bypass mandatory controls. All claim decisions and reviewer actions must remain auditable.

Measures of Success:
- Reduce average review time by 30%.
- Resolve 90% of eligible low-risk claims within 2 business days.
- Keep manual rework below 5%.
- Ensure high-risk claims require human review.
- Preserve end-to-end auditability.
output:
Title: Accelerate Claims Triage and Review

Description:
Introduce a consistent claims triage and review workflow that categorizes incoming claims by risk and complexity, fast-tracks eligible low-risk claims, and ensures suspicious or high-risk claims are reviewed by a senior reviewer. Reviewers will have a prioritized work queue showing risk category, aging, missing information, and escalation reason. The workflow will preserve existing policy and fraud systems as systems of record and maintain a complete audit trail.

Success Criteria:
- Average claims review time is reduced by 30%.
- At least 90% of eligible low-risk claims receive a decision within 2 business days.
- Manual rework remains below 5%.
- High-risk claims cannot be automatically approved and require human review.
- Reviewers can see risk category, aging, missing documents, and escalation reasons.
- Reviewers can add notes and reassign claims.
- Customers are notified when claims are received, when more information is required, and when a decision is made.
- Customer messages do not expose internal fraud-scoring logic.
- Claim decisions and reviewer actions remain auditable.

context:
Theme ID: THEME-003
Theme Name: Supplier Onboarding and Compliance Standardization

Theme Summary:
Supplier onboarding differs across procurement teams and regions, resulting in inconsistent data quality, long cycle times, and repeated support requests. The organization needs a standardized supplier onboarding experience that improves speed while retaining compliance controls.

Business Need:
Suppliers should enter company, tax, banking, and contact information through a single guided experience. Tax and banking information should be validated before activation. Suppliers should be able to save a partially completed onboarding request and return later. Procurement users should be able to see the supplier's onboarding status and any blocking issues.

Compliance Expectations:
Required sanctions, tax, and banking validations must complete before a supplier can become active. Failed validations should be routed for review rather than silently rejected. The system should retain evidence of validation results and approval activity.

Operational Expectations:
Average supplier onboarding time should be reduced by 35%. Onboarding-related support tickets should be reduced by 25%. Duplicate supplier records should be reduced by checking for existing suppliers before creating a new record.

Communication:
Suppliers should receive confirmation when onboarding is submitted, notification when additional information is required, and notification when onboarding is approved or rejected. Rejection messages should provide a clear reason where policy permits.

Constraints:
The existing ERP remains the system of record for active suppliers. No supplier should be activated if mandatory compliance checks are incomplete. Procurement teams must use the common workflow rather than region-specific spreadsheets.

Measures of Success:
- Reduce supplier onboarding time by 35%.
- Reduce onboarding support tickets by 25%.
- Validate tax and banking details before activation.
- Prevent duplicate supplier creation where an existing supplier is detected.
- Preserve compliance review and evidence.

Suppliers can save progress and resume later, while procurement users can see onboarding status and blocking issues. The ERP remains the system of record for active suppliers.

Theme ID: THEME-004
Theme Name: Employee Access Request Experience

Theme Summary:
Employees currently request application access through email, chat, and separate ticket forms. Approval paths are inconsistent, requesters lack status visibility, and fulfillment teams receive incomplete information.

Business Need:
Employees should request application access through a self-service experience. The request should capture the application, access role, business justification, and requested duration when temporary access is needed. Standard requests should be routed to the employee's manager for approval and then to the appropriate fulfillment process.

User Experience:
Employees should be able to see current request status, pending approver, and completed steps. They should be notified when a request is approved, rejected, canceled, or requires more information. Rejection messages should include a reason.

Operational Expectations:
Standard access requests should be completed within 1 business day after all required approvals are received. Duplicate requests for the same user/application/role combination should be prevented. Fulfillment teams should receive complete request details and approval evidence.

Security and Governance:
Privileged roles require an additional security approval. Temporary access should include an expiration date. Existing identity-governance policies must remain authoritative. The workflow must record approval and fulfillment activity for audit.

Constraints:
The solution must not automatically grant privileged access without required security approval. Existing directory and identity-governance platforms remain systems of record.

Measures of Success:
- Standard access completion within 1 business day after approval.
- Improved employee visibility into status and pending actions.
- Reduced duplicate and incomplete requests.
- Preserved approval and audit controls.

input:

context:
Theme ID: THEME-005
Theme Name: Payment Failure Recovery and Checkout Resilience

Theme Summary:
Customers frequently abandon checkout after a payment failure because error messages are unclear and retries require restarting portions of the checkout flow. Support teams also receive avoidable contacts about failed transactions.

Business Need:
When a payment fails, the customer should receive a clear, actionable failure message when the payment provider supplies an explainable reason. The customer should be able to retry payment without re-entering unaffected checkout data. Where supported, the customer should be able to choose an alternate payment method without restarting checkout.

Operational Expectations:
Payment failure rate should be reduced by 20%. Successful checkout completion after an initial payment failure should increase by 15%. Payment-related support contacts should be reduced by 25%.

Customer Communication:
The customer should know whether a retry is safe, whether the prior attempt may still be processing, and when a retry succeeds. The experience must avoid implying that a charge failed when the transaction status is uncertain.

Risk and Compliance:
Existing fraud and payment-provider controls must remain in effect. The application must not bypass risk declines. Sensitive card data must not be written to logs or user-visible error details.

Constraints:
The existing payment gateway remains in place for the first release. The solution must support web and mobile checkout experiences.

Measures of Success:
- Reduce payment failure rate by 20%.
- Increase successful checkout completion after an initial failure by 15%.
- Reduce payment-related support contacts by 25%.
- Preserve fraud controls and secure handling of payment data.
output:
Title: Improve Payment Failure Recovery

Description:
Improve checkout resilience by giving customers clear and actionable payment failure messages when explainable reasons are available, preserving unaffected checkout data, and allowing customers to retry or select an alternate payment method without restarting checkout. The experience will clearly distinguish a confirmed failure from a transaction whose status is still uncertain. Existing fraud controls and the current payment gateway will remain in place. The team will use a Redis-backed retry-state service to maintain recovery context.

Success Criteria:
- Payment failure rate is reduced by 20%.
- Successful checkout completion after an initial failure increases by 15%.
- Payment-related support contacts are reduced by 25%.
- Customers receive actionable failure messages when the provider supplies an explainable reason.
- Customers can retry without re-entering unaffected checkout information.
- Customers can choose an alternate supported payment method without restarting checkout.

Theme ID: THEME-005
Theme Name: Payment Failure Recovery and Checkout Resilience

Theme Summary:
Customers frequently abandon checkout after a payment failure because error messages are unclear and retries require restarting portions of the checkout flow. Support teams also receive avoidable contacts about failed transactions.

Business Need:
When a payment fails, the customer should receive a clear, actionable failure message when the payment provider supplies an explainable reason. The customer should be able to retry payment without re-entering unaffected checkout data. Where supported, the customer should be able to choose an alternate payment method without restarting checkout.

Operational Expectations:
Payment failure rate should be reduced by 20%. Successful checkout completion after an initial payment failure should increase by 15%. Payment-related support contacts should be reduced by 25%.

Customer Communication:
The customer should know whether a retry is safe, whether the prior attempt may still be processing, and when a retry succeeds. The experience must avoid implying that a charge failed when the transaction status is uncertain.

Risk and Compliance:
Existing fraud and payment-provider controls must remain in effect. The application must not bypass risk declines. Sensitive card data must not be written to logs or user-visible error details.

Constraints:
The existing payment gateway remains in place for the first release. The solution must support web and mobile checkout experiences.

Measures of Success:
- Reduce payment failure rate by 20%.
- Increase successful checkout completion after an initial failure by 15%.
- Reduce payment-related support contacts by 25%.
- Preserve fraud controls and secure handling of payment data.
